sources.terms_note: Public EDGAR data. SEC fair-access policy: a User-Agent that names the requester and a contact (ours does) and at most 10 requests per second; this is one request a day. Each row [cik, name, ticker, exchange] becomes one instrument item: the company's name, ticker, exchange and CIK as SEC lists them. Informational only: no advice, no execution (ADR-025). Needs SOURCES_MAX_ITEMS_PER_FETCH of at least 11000 (about 10,450 rows in October 2026).
sources.license_note: US government work: public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Cite 'U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission'.

sources.name: Frankfurter euro reference rates

sources.terms_note: Frankfurter is MIT-licensed software, free for commercial use, with no API key and no quota (only anti-abuse rate limiting). The rates themselves fall under each provider's terms, so attribute the contributing provider (ECB, TCMB, ...) and link https://frankfurter.dev/ and the provider's terms; for ECB-sourced rates cite 'European Central Bank'. The legacy object endpoint https://api.frankfurter.app/latest cannot be mapped by the api adapter (it requires an array at items_path), so the array endpoint https://api.frankfurter.dev/v2/rates is used and each row (date, base, quote, rate) becomes one item. Rates are informational observations only, never advice (ADR-025). Re-verify before enabling.
sources.license_note: Frankfurter software: MIT. Underlying rates: per provider (ECB reference rates reusable with attribution); see https://frankfurter.dev/license/.

sources.name: Vultr cloud plans
sources.robots_note: robots.txt checked 2026-10-11: https://api.vultr.com/robots.txt is exactly 'User-agent: *' followed by 'Disallow: /', which disallows every path on the API host. The fetcher re-checks robots.txt on every run and would refuse /v2/plans as disallowed, so this source cannot be enabled as written — an operator must resolve the robots.txt block with Vultr first. (The endpoint itself answers without an API key.)
sources.terms_note: Vultr's API documentation says the plans listing needs no API key for ordinary accounts ('If your account has special plans available, you will need to pass your API key ... For all other accounts, the API key is not required'), and the official govultr client documents that 'public operations like listing plans ... will still work' unauthenticated; /v2/plans answered with plan data to our keyless fetcher. www.vultr.com/api/ and www.vultr.com/legal/tos/ both answered 403 to our fetcher, so Vultr's API terms could not be read here and must be read by a person before enabling. Attribute Vultr by linking https://www.vultr.com/pricing/; show each price as an observation 'checked on <date>', never a current price, and imply no endorsement. Re-verify before enabling.
sources.license_note: Plan specifications and prices are Vultr's data (https://www.vultr.com/pricing/); Vultr's terms pages could not be fetched (HTTP 403 to our fetcher) and no licence to republish them was found. Attribute Vultr and link the pricing page; no endorsement implied.

sources.terms_note: Akamai's Linode API documentation says 'Some of this API's operations are publicly accessible and don't require authentication'; /v4/linode/types answered with type data to our keyless fetcher. https://www.linode.com/legal-tos/ answers 404 and https://www.linode.com/legal redirects to https://www.akamai.com/legal, where the governing documents are Akamai's Acceptable Use Policy and the Akamai Cloud (Linode) Master Services Agreement; none of those pages states a right to, or a clear ban on, republishing plan or price data (the AUP forbids using the network to build a competitive service and IP infringement), so a person must read them before enabling. Attribute Akamai/Linode by linking https://www.linode.com/pricing/; show each price as an observation 'checked on <date>', never a current price, and imply no endorsement. Re-verify before enabling.

sources.name: OVHcloud VPS plans (US catalog)
sources.robots_note: robots.txt checked 2026-10-15: https://api.us.ovhcloud.com/robots.txt answers 404 (nginx), and api.ovh.com/robots.txt redirects to https://api.eu.ovhcloud.com/robots.txt, also 404, so the API hosts publish no robots.txt rules; a 404 is treated as no restrictions (never guessed as a disallow). The fetcher re-checks robots.txt on every run. (us.ovhcloud.com, the marketing site, is a different host and is not fetched.)
sources.terms_note: OVHcloud's own API schema (https://api.us.ovhcloud.com/1.0/order.json) marks GET /order/catalog/public/vps 'noAuthentication': true with apiStatus 'Stable production version' ('Retrieve VPS catalog'): the public catalog is meant to be read without an account, and it answered our keyless fetcher. OVHcloud's general terms (https://us.ovhcloud.com/legal/) govern its services; no page found states a right to, or a ban on, republishing catalog prices, so a person reads them before enabling. One file (about 12 MB, mostly operating-system options) a day. Prices are the catalog's integers in hundred-millionths of the currency (535000000 is $5.35); show each as an observation 'checked on <date>' with a link to https://us.ovhcloud.com/vps/, never a quote, and imply no endorsement. Only the current plan codes (vps-<year>-model<n>, US datacenters) are kept: the -eu/-ca region copies, local-zone (.LZ) plans, commitment discounts and legacy upgrade codes are filtered out. Re-verify before enabling.
sources.license_note: Plan specifications and prices are OVHcloud's data (https://us.ovhcloud.com/vps/). No licence to republish them was found beyond the public catalog being offered without authentication. Attribute OVHcloud and link the VPS page; no endorsement implied.
